question.text: Ms. Neha Kapoor, CIO of Nilgiri Multi-Strategy Fund (Cat III), targets a real risk-free component of 2.00% and expects 6.00% inflation over the coming year. She wants to quote the nominal risk-free benchmark to compute the fund's equity risk premium. Per the NISM Fisher formulation, what is the exact nominal risk-free rate (to 2 decimal places)?

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 1.4.1 worked example: Nominal Risk-free Rate = (1 + Real) x (1 + Inflation) - 1 = (1.02 x 1.06) - 1 = 1.0812 - 1 = 8.12%. This is identical to the chapter's 2% real plus 6% inflation example yielding 8.12% nominal. The Trap: Option A is the primary trap — additive Real + Inflation = 8.00% ignores the 0.12% cross-product (2% x 6% = 0.12%). The chapter emphasises this cross-product because at higher inflation it becomes material. Option B is a reversed-subtraction distractor; Option D is nonsensical. Note: The chapter also covers Sharpe ratio (pages 191-192), where the nominal risk-free rate computed via Fisher feeds in as the risk-free reference.
